# Bet Canvas & Company OKRs

Owner: **CEO**. Every significant initiative is framed as a *bet* — a hypothesis with a budget (in runway) and a written kill condition — before it reaches the Product Manager for discovery. If you can't write the kill condition, you don't understand the bet yet.

## Bet Canvas

```markdown
# Bet: [Name]
**Owner**: [PM who runs discovery]   **Decision date**: [date]

## Hypothesis
If we [do X] for [customer segment], they will [behavior / pay], because [insight].

## Why now
Market signal, competitive pressure, or capability shift that makes this the moment.

## Budget
**Runway allocated**: [N weeks of team-time + $ infra/model spend]
**Team committed**: [which agents, what % capacity]

## Success signal (advance the bet)
The specific, measurable evidence — paying pilot, activation %, retention — that justifies more funding.

## Kill condition (stop the bet)
The specific signal that says stop. No kill condition → not ready to fund.

## Strategic fit
Which company OKR this serves. If none, why are we doing it?
```

## Build / Partner / Buy / Kill

| Question | Build | Partner / Buy | Kill / Defer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Core differentiation? | Yes — own it | No — plumbing | No — and no one pays |
| Runway to learn? | Yes, funded | Partner to skip build | Out of runway |
| Paying-customer signal? | Strong | Enough to integrate | Weak after a real test |
| Compounds our advantage? | Yes | Accelerates us | No |

**Rule:** Build only what is core differentiation AND has signal AND fits runway. Else partner, wait, or kill.

## Company OKR

```markdown
# Company OKRs — [Quarter Year]
**Runway at start**: [N weeks]   **North Star**: [single metric of company health]

## Objective 1: [qualitative, ambitious, time-boxed]
- KR1: [metric] from [baseline] to [target]
- KR2: [metric] from [baseline] to [target]
- Owner: [PM or CTO]   Bet(s): [linked Bet Canvas]

## Explicitly NOT this quarter
- [tempting initiative we are deliberately not funding] — revisit when [condition]
```
